checks.invariant: Policy.decide on an agent exec command costs a small bounded amount of CPU before the call is rejected or queued. A length cap sits before decide.
checks.result: No per-command or per-argument length cap exists. ToolCall.args is an unbounded dict (api.py:54-55), and the only limit is _BodyLimit max_body_bytes, 8 MiB (config.py:65). The route runs box.call_tool on the shared 32-thread tool_pool (api.py:160, 277-278). call_tool admits 4 per sandbox (service.py:286-290). _call_tool writes the tool_request audit row and then calls policy.decide (service.py:309-311), before the pending-approval cap (service.py:326). Measured in sbx (Python 3.13, 1 CPU), default policy, 'x;'*n: 16/32/64/128 KiB took 0.64/1.32/2.59/4.85 s. 'x|' gave the same. 'a '*n took 0.025-0.20 s, and 'rm a a ...' took 0.014-0.108 s. Growth is linear, not superlinear, but the constant is large: about 38 us per shell-punctuation token. cProfile shows command_names to _words taking 2.30 of 2.53 s. _words builds a new shlex for every token that contains punctuation, even a bare ';' (policy.py:45, 60-61), and shlex.__init__ plus str.translate account for 1.0 s and 0.78 s. has_bash_comment (0.008 s), simple_programs (0.096 s), _raw_hits (0.002 s) and _split_segments (0.099 s) at 64 KiB are minor. Linear extrapolation gives about 310 s of GIL-holding CPU for one 8 MiB call.

checks.invariant: While agent policy evaluation runs, other Python threads in the same process (event loop, human request threads) stay responsive.
checks.result: An asyncio stand-in loop in the main thread ran a fixed small CPU unit plus a 1 ms sleep, 40 times. Baseline: median 2.2 ms, max 2.7 ms, total 0.09 s. With 1 concurrent Policy.decide('x;'*65536, i.e. 128 KiB): median 7.5 ms, max 10.1 ms, total 0.31 s. With 4 concurrent (the per-sandbox tool_concurrency default): median 8.6 ms, max 88.8 ms, total 0.90 s, and each decide's wall time stretched from 5.6 s to about 24.9 s. The GIL switch interval is 5 ms, so other threads are slowed in proportion to the number of runnable decide threads (about 4x median, 33x max with one agent's 4 slots), not frozen. Several sandboxes' agents would add up to 32 tool_pool threads.

checks.invariant: Preview of a REQUIRE_APPROVAL exec command costs a bounded number of container execs and a bounded amount of exec time before the approval is created.
checks.result: _call_tool calls _preview (service.py:331-332) to SandboxManager.preview (sandbox.py:584-587) to preview_command. For every rm operand, preview calls expand(op) (preview.py:88-89), and for every match under -r it calls walk(m, limit) (preview.py:96). Each of these is one synchronous docker exec_run with no container-side timeout (_expand sandbox.py:568-574, _walk sandbox.py:576-582), unlike the _timed manifest/read execs. 'limit' only truncates 'affected' after all execs have run (preview.py:126-128). Counted with stub callbacks: 'rm -r d d ...' at 16 KiB gave 8189 expand + 8189 walk calls; at 64 KiB, 32765 + 32765. 'rm -r *' over 5000 workspace entries gave 1 expand + 5000 walk calls. Scaled to the 8 MiB cap, that is about 4.2M expand plus 4.2M walk execs, run serially on one tool_pool thread, with no deadline and no cancellation on client disconnect. The real per-exec latency and Docker-daemon impact need the live daemon (not available in sbx).

checks.invariant: Preview output and the approval-card render of an agent command stay bounded in memory and size.
checks.result: preview_command appends one note per unrecognised segment with no cap (preview.py:122-125). Measured: 32/128/512 KiB 'x;' commands gave 16384/65536/262144 notes and preview JSON of 1.46/5.83/23.3 MB, a constant 44.5x. tracemalloc peak was 14.8/59.4 MiB at 128/512 KiB, which extrapolates to about 950 MiB for 8 MiB. ApprovalStore.create json.dumps the raw preview into the pending row (approvals.py:49-59). _approvals.html renders every note (line 16) and the full command (line 8) for pending rows. The audit copy is bounded by bound_payload (audit.py:141-152). This is the same root cause, and the same remediation (a NOTES_MAX cap in preview.py), as the already-filed h-approvals finding agentbox/audit.py:append:agent-grown-rows-in-shared-sqlite-have-no-aggregate-bound-or-retention, which measured the 5832767-byte preview and the 7.47 MB card. It is consolidated there, not re-filed.

candidates.title: Agent exec command of up to 8 MiB drives minutes of GIL-holding policy parsing per call, slowing the shared control plane
candidates.description: An agent token can POST /sandboxes/{sid}/tools/exec with a command of shell-punctuation tokens (e.g. 'x;x;x;...') up to the 8 MiB AGENTBOX_MAX_BODY. No per-command length cap exists anywhere before Policy.decide. With the default policy, command_names calls _words, which constructs a new shlex.shlex for every token that contains a punctuation character, including each bare ';'. That costs about 38 us per token: 4.85 s for 128 KiB, linear, so about 310 s for one 8 MiB call. The work runs on the shared tool_pool and holds the process GIL. One agent can keep 4 such calls running (tool_concurrency). The run happens before the pending-approval cap, so that cap does not stop it. A stand-in event-loop thread slowed from 2.2 ms median / 2.7 ms max to 8.6 ms median / 88.8 ms max while 4 calls ran, and each call's wall time stretched to about 25 s. The control plane degrades (it is not frozen) for every human request and every other sandbox for as long as the agent re-issues calls.
candidates.root_cause: Policy evaluation has no input-size bound. AgentBox.call_tool/_call_tool pass args['command'] of any length to Policy.decide (service.py:311). The only limit is the 8 MiB HTTP body cap. _words (policy.py:40-62) re-lexes every token that contains a shell punctuation or whitespace character with a fresh shlex.shlex instance (policy.py:45, 60-61). shlex.__init__ is expensive (str.translate of wordchars), so cost is about 38 us per punctuation token, and an 8 MiB command holds about 4M such tokens.
candidates.intended_behavior: An agent-supplied command or argument longer than a small fixed bound (e.g. 64 KiB) is rejected (400/413) or sent straight to REQUIRE_APPROVAL without full parsing, before policy.decide and preview run. _words does not re-lex tokens made only of punctuation, so evaluation costs at most milliseconds and human requests keep their normal latency.

trace.description: An agent token posts {"args":{"command":"x;"*N}}. ToolCall.args is an unbounded dict (api.py:54-55), limited only by _BodyLimit at 8 MiB (config.py:65).
Dispatched to the shared 32-thread tool_pool (api.py:160) via run_in_executor. A client disconnect does not cancel the job.
Admits up to tool_concurrency (4) concurrent calls per sandbox, with no size check.
policy.decide(tool, args) runs after the tool_request audit row and before the pending-approval cap (service.py:326).
The rm-curl-needs-approval rule (default_policy.yaml:12-17) calls command_names(cmd) on the whole command.
Each token containing a punctuation char (every ';') is recursively re-lexed with a new shlex instance (policy.py:45). This is about 38 us per token, holding the GIL.

evidence.description: Recursion condition: any token with whitespace or a char in _SHELL_PUNCT, including a bare ';' token, triggers _words(t, depth+1), which builds a new shlex (line 45).
decide is called with the raw command. No length check exists in call_tool/_call_tool (service.py:279-311). grep finds no command-length constant in agentbox/.
max_body_bytes defaults to 8 MiB, the only bound on the command length.
Per-sandbox tool_concurrency (default 4) allows 4 concurrent evaluations per agent. tool_pool has 32 workers across sandboxes (api.py:160).

conditions.description: Requires the sandbox's agent token, which is the lowest-trust principal and is assumed prompt-injected by the threat model.
Default AGENTBOX_MAX_BODY (8 MiB), default policy with an exec 'commands' rule (rm-curl-needs-approval), default tool_concurrency 4.

execution.attacker_perspective: A prompt-injected agent holding its own sandbox's agent token repeatedly sends exec tool calls whose command is a long run of 'x;' tokens. Each call is eventually queued as an approval (or 429 by the pending cap), but only after Policy.decide has consumed CPU in proportion to the command length.
instructions: In the parent-approved sbx (no network, uid 65534, 512 MiB, 1 CPU, 120 s, audited source read-only at /target), load the default policy with agentbox.policy.Policy.load and time Policy.decide('exec', {'command': s}) for s = 'x;'*n at 16/32/64/128 KiB, plus 'x|', 'a ' and 'rm a a ...' shapes. Profile the 16 KiB case with cProfile.

In the same harness, run an asyncio probe on the main thread (40 iterations of a fixed 20000-step Python loop plus await asyncio.sleep(0.001)) alone, with 1 thread, and with 4 threads each running decide on the 128 KiB 'x;' command. Record median, max and total probe latency and each decide's wall time.
execution.observed_result: decide('x;' * n): 16 KiB 0.641 s, 32 KiB 1.318 s, 64 KiB 2.593 s, 128 KiB 4.845 s (linear, ~38 us per token). 'x|' was the same, 'a ' 0.199 s at 128 KiB, and 'rm a a...' 0.108 s at 128 KiB. cProfile: command_names to _words took 2.30 of 2.53 s, with 65538 shlex.__init__ calls (1.02 s) and str.translate (0.78 s). Probe baseline median 2.2 ms / max 2.7 ms / total 0.09 s. With 1 decide thread: 7.5 / 10.1 ms / 0.31 s. With 4 decide threads: 8.6 / 88.8 ms / 0.90 s, and each decide's wall time stretched to 24.3-25.0 s. Extrapolation: about 310 s CPU for one 8 MiB call (not run). (agents/h-policy-cpu/artifacts/h.out, agents/h-policy-cpu/artifacts/h2.out)

remediation.strategy: Bound the input before any parsing, and remove the per-token re-lex. In AgentBox._call_tool (before the tool_request audit row and policy.decide), refuse an exec command or any string argument longer than a fixed TOOL_ARG_MAX (e.g. 64 KiB) with 413/400 and a tool_blocked audit row. Alternatively, route it directly to REQUIRE_APPROVAL with a fixed 'too long to analyse' preview, skipping command_names and preview_command. In _words, skip recursion for tokens made only of punctuation and recurse only on tokens that contain whitespace or '$(' or '`'. Add a regression test asserting that decide on a 64 KiB 'x;' command finishes in under ~100 ms and that a 1 MiB command is rejected or approval-routed without calling command_names.

likelihood.reason: A single agent-token request with a default configuration triggers it, and a prompt-injected agent can repeat it indefinitely. No approval or human action is needed first.

impact.reason: Measured effect is degradation, not denial. One agent's 4 concurrent calls slowed a same-process stand-in loop about 4x at the median and up to 33x at the max, for minutes per call at the body cap. The control plane keeps answering, and the effect ends when the calls finish. Several hostile sandboxes would worsen it, but that was not measured.

confidence.reason: The CPU cost, linear growth and GIL contention were measured directly on the audited code with the default policy. The real server's latency under uvicorn on the host's CPU count, and the full 8 MiB figure, are extrapolated, not observed.

candidates.title: Approval preview runs one untimed docker exec per rm operand and per matched path, with no count or deadline, before the approval exists
candidates.description: For any exec command that needs approval and contains an rm segment, preview_command calls expand(op) once per operand and, with -r, walk(m) once per expanded match. Each call is a synchronous docker exec_run in SandboxManager._expand/_walk with no container-side timeout. The 'limit' (200) truncates only the displayed 'affected' list after every exec has run. An agent can send 'rm -r d d d ...' (about 4.2M operands at the 8 MiB body cap; 32765 at 64 KiB) or create many files with the allowed 'touch' and send 'rm -r *' (one walk exec per entry). One tool_pool thread then serially drives that many docker API exec create/start/inspect round trips against the shared host Docker daemon, with no deadline, before the 202 is returned. Cancelling the client request does not stop it.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: preview_command (preview.py:88-98) loops over every operand and every match and calls the container callbacks without a call budget, total deadline or early stop once 'limit' affected entries exist. _expand (sandbox.py:568-574) and _walk (sandbox.py:576-582) use plain exec_run without the _timed wrapper used by the manifest and read execs. Neither _call_tool nor call_tool caps the operand count or the command length (service.py:279-332).

trace.description: An agent token posts {"args":{"command":"rm -r d d d ..."}} up to 8 MiB. It runs on the shared tool_pool (api.py:278).
The decision is REQUIRE_APPROVAL (rm-curl-needs-approval). After the pending cap check (line 326), _preview to sandboxes.preview (service.py:226) runs synchronously before approvals.create.
preview_command is called with lambdas bound to _expand/_walk on the live container.
expand(op) runs for every operand. walk(m, limit) runs for every match when recursive (line 96). There is no budget, and the limit is applied only at lines 126-128.
Each call is c.exec_run(['sh','-c',...]) with no timeout (also _walk at line 577): one docker exec per operand/match.

evidence.description: items = walk(m, limit) if recursive else [m], called per match inside the per-operand loop. limit bounds only each walk's output, not the number of walks.
Truncation to 'limit' happens after all expand/walk execs have completed.
_expand exec_run has no _timed wrapper or container-side timeout, unlike the manifest exec (sandbox.py:376).
touch and mkdir are in the allow-listed read-only-exec set, so the agent can populate /workspace with many entries without approval before sending 'rm -r *'.

blockers: The real latency and host-side cost of each docker exec_run (exec_create, exec_start, exec_inspect) against the Docker daemon, and whether millions of serial execs measurably delay other sandboxes' tool calls or human lifecycle/approval actions that also use the daemon, need the real Docker daemon. The sbx has no Docker socket. Only call counts were observed locally (stub callbacks: 32765 expand + 32765 walk calls for a 64 KiB 'rm -r d d ...' command; 5000 walk calls for 'rm -r *' over 5000 entries; agents/h-policy-cpu/artifacts/h2.out).

validation_plan.local: In a disposable loopback control plane (dummy human/agent tokens, default policy, one runc sandbox from ubuntu:24.04): (1) with the agent token, POST /sandboxes/{sid}/tools/exec with command 'rm -r ' + 'd '*2000 after 'mkdir d' (allowed). Measure the wall time until the 202 and count exec events with 'docker events --filter type=container --filter event=exec_start' (expect about 4000). (2) Repeat with 'touch f1 ... f2000' then 'rm -r *' (expect 2000 walk execs). (3) While (1) runs, time a human GET /sandboxes and a POST /sandboxes/{other}/tools/exec 'ls' from a second sandbox, and compare with baseline. Extrapolate the per-exec latency to the 8 MiB operand count. Stop at the first measurable delay; do not run 8 MiB inputs.

hardening: call_tool's executor job is not cancelled when the HTTP client disconnects (api.py:277-278), so a long decide or preview keeps its tool_pool thread and _busy slot to completion even after the sandbox is deleted.

_raw_hits (policy.py:164-170), has_bash_comment (policy.py:85-125), simple_programs and _split_segments are linear with small constants (0.002-0.1 s at 64 KiB). Nested quoting depth is capped at 4 (_words) and 3 (_split_segments), so recursion multiplies cost by at most about 5x. No superlinear path was found.

The unbounded per-segment preview notes (preview.py:122-125; 44.5x JSON amplification, about 950 MiB estimated Python memory at 8 MiB) and the uncapped _approvals.html render of pending rows (line 16) share the remediation already attached to the filed h-approvals fingerprint (NOTES_MAX in preview_command). A TOOL_ARG_MAX before decide would also bound them.
